resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA New Hampshire list gives the tower as relocated from AL. The 2022 chapter report says Davana did not answer where it was removed from. The story reports the list's claim as the list's claim and does not treat the Alabama origin as confirmed.

notes_for_editor: The 2022 chapter report and the FFLA New Hampshire list are the only sources read. Both date from 2022 or are undated, so the current condition and access are unknown; the story says so. The brief's events were garbled: '2022 built' is corrected to a relocation and erection, and 'None relocated' contradicted 'Moved from Alabama'. The FFLA list says 'Relocated from AL'; the 2022 report says the seller has not said where the tower came from, so the Alabama origin stays attributed to the list. Two searches found no other source naming the earlier site. A Davana sale-list PDF (DAVANA-LLC-0725.pdf) was read in part for context; the matched lines do not mention Hooksett or Bass Pro. The coordinates match the brief (43.04077, -71.47663). About six page reads and two searches were used for this tower. Fact check 2026-10-09: the story said the 2022 report 'says something different'; it only fails to confirm the Alabama origin, so the wording now says that. The story also said all sources date from 2022; the FFLA New Hampshire list has no date, so the story now says the report dates from 2022 and the list is undated. Both pages were read in full and the quotes were confirmed.
